bugs.error_message: User: 'Set Up Sharing hangs on the spinning icon, unable to press Done'; share was actually created (visible after force-quit)
bugs.root_cause: NSPersistentCloudKitContainer.share(_:to:) does blocking work on its calling thread, and under SWIFT_APPROACHABLE_CONCURRENCY (nonisolated(nonsending) caller's-actor semantics) the awaited async import ran it ON the main actor — freezing UI and deadlocking against completion delivery. Server record was created before the deadlock, hence post-restart visibility.
bugs.fix: createShare now wraps the completion-handler share(_:to:completion:) and persistUpdatedShare(_:in:completion:) in Task.detached + withCheckedThrowingContinuation, so all container work happens off the main actor; only the @Published share assignment returns to main.

bugs.error_message: User: after Stop Sharing, reopening the Household sheet shows sharing active again; correct only after app restart
bugs.root_cause: fetchShares(matching:) reads the LOCAL share cache, which keeps the deleted CKShare until the next mirroring import. Each sheet presentation created a fresh @StateObject SharingController that trusted the stale cache.
bugs.fix: SharingController is now a session singleton (SharingController.shared, @ObservedObject in HouseholdView) and tracks deletedShareRecordIDs; loadShare treats any cached share whose recordID is in that set as gone. stopSharing and leaveHousehold both record the deleted ID.

bugs.error_message: Release-config warnings: 'call to main actor-isolated static method normalize in a synchronous nonisolated context' (CategoryClassifier x2) + weak/strong capture warning in SharingController observer
bugs.root_cause: nonisolated on a class declaration does NOT extend to members declared in its extensions — they get the project's MainActor default, so GroceryItem.normalize was MainActor while its callers (nonisolated CategoryClassifier) were not. Swift 5 mode made it a warning, but it's an error in Swift 6 mode and a latent misisolation. The observer closure also implicitly strong-captured self alongside an inner weak capture (retain until observer removal).
bugs.fix: Marked normalize and foldTrailingPlural explicitly nonisolated; observer closure now [weak self] with early unwrap to a local strong ref passed into the MainActor Task. Release device build now has zero warnings. Note: [self] capture-list + implicit member refs does NOT satisfy 'explicit use of self' in Swift 5 mode — use a named local instead.
